assumptions: X={0,...,n-1} is finite; n=0 allowed. T is any total self-map, not necessarily bijective.
N>=1 and labels are fixed elements of Z/NZ; distinct functions are counted without quotienting by phase.
Defect counts vertices x with f(T(x)) != f(x)+1 mod N; all edges have equal unit weight.
Unconstrained minimization does not impose surjectivity. A factor requires exact equivariance and surjectivity; approximate surjective labelings are distinguished.
Every nonempty functional-graph component has one directed cycle and incoming trees.
No ASM, rowmotion, PL or birational dynamics are constructed; no new resonance definition or parent solution claimed.
target: Determine the minimum number and number of minimum-defect cyclic labelings of an arbitrary finite self-map, and falsify the claim that an optimal labeling must be surjective when the domain is large enough.
